title: Acid-Base Titration Workbench
aim: Determine the concentration of an unknown hydrochloric acid solution by titration against standard sodium hydroxide solution using phenolphthalein indicator.
theory: Neutralization titration involves reactively mixing an acid and base to reach stoichiometry (equivalence). HCl + NaOH -> NaCl + H2O. Phenolphthalein turns pink at the alkaline endpoint (pH ~8.3).
procedure: Fill the burette with 0.1M sodium hydroxide titrant.
Pipette 10 mL of unknown HCl analyte into conical flask.
Run titrant drop-wise while swirling until faint pink color persists.
Record the burette volume equivalence mark.
observations: Local pink color appears and disappears upon swirling.
Faint persistent pink coloration marks the equivalence titration volume endpoint.
result: Stoichiometry pH equivalence successfully reached and titration volume recorded.

viva_questions.question: What is the equivalent point in a titration?
viva_questions.answer: The point at which the added titrant is stoichiometrically equal to the analyte.

viva_questions.question: Why does phenolphthalein turn pink in basic solutions?
viva_questions.answer: Deprotonation of phenolphthalein shifts its chemical structure, widening the conjugation and absorbing green light to reflect pink.
